notes: Access: direct fetch worked throughout (HTTP 200, no WAF); robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (generic Shopify agent-access policy, UCP/MCP mentioned but not required). Shopify storefront confirmed (ikiru.in myshopify backend). Rule 1 applied hard: products_count field NOT used anywhere -- every qty is an exact unique-product-ID count from paging /collections/<handle>/products.json?limit=250 to exhaustion. 943 total collections exist on the site (via /collections.json); the vast majority are furniture, kitchen appliances/cookware/cutlery, bar tools, textiles, bedding, home fragrance, bathroom fixtures/storage, office supplies, and misc utility/storage collections that are out of SCOPE and were excluded after reviewing the full site nav (400 nav links extracted) and spot-checking product titles. Duplicate-company determination: no other 'Ikiru' home decor company found in this project's prior batches; this looks like a first-time entry, no evidence of prior extraction under a different S.N. Roll-up handling: 'Mirrors' and 'Decorative Mirror' landing collections were dropped as overlapping roll-ups of Wall Mirror + Floor Mirror (kept as the two clean leaves). 'Clocks' landing collection (110) exactly equals Table Clock(75)+Wall Clock(35), confirmed pure roll-up, dropped. 'Wall decor' (302) and 'Decor Objects' (703) are broad mixed roll-ups overlapping many of the specific leaves already counted (bowls, showpieces, clocks, bookends, wall art, photo frames all appeared inside 'Decor Objects' title samples) -- both dropped per the mixed-roll-up rule to avoid double counting; their genuine component product types are captured individually (Vase, Showpieces & Collectibles, Bookends, Globes, Photo Frames, Religious Idols, Table Clock, Decorative Wall Plates, etc). Rule 0 gains: Ashtrays (decorative brass/crystal, explicitly marketed as home decor, not smoking accessories), Tissue & Napkin Boxes (brass/glass/marble decorative tabletop boxes), Diya & Diya Stands and Urli Bowls (candle-holder / decorative-bowl product types despite Pooja-room association), Religious Idols and Religious Paintings & Prints (figurine and wall-art product types despite religious subject matter) were all INCLUDED under Rule 0 (product type beats room/occasion name) rather than being excluded for their religious/room association. Excluded per SCOPE: Home Fragrance (Candles/Aroma Oil Diffusers/Incense -- 'candles' collection is dominated by scented candles, kept separate from the unscented 'Candle Stand' holders collection which IS included), Cushion & Cushion Covers / Rugs & Carpets / Table Runner / Bedding (textiles), Dried Flowers & Fragrance (faux botanicals + fragrance), Christmas Decoration Items and Festive Gifting (Holiday & Gift), all Furniture collections (TV Unit, Tables, Chairs, Sofas, Beds, Wardrobe, Cabinets, Pooja Chowki, Trunk, Plant Stand -- furniture-type stands/pedestals), Cutlery & Cutlery Holder / Barware Accessories / Cookware / Kitchen Utilities (kitchen tools & cutlery), Key Holder and Napkin Rings (functional hardware; the Napkin Rings collection was in fact miscategorized -- its single listed product is a cutlery set), Home Storage Organizer tree (Waste Bin, Coat Stand, Hooks, Laundry, Bathroom Cabinet/Mats/Towels -- functional storage/fixtures), Office Desk Accessories / Office Decor pen-stand items, Toilet Paper Holder / Towel Holder Stand / Bathroom Dispensers & Sets / Other Bath Accessories (functional bathroom fixtures, kept only the genuinely decorative Soap Dish), Pooja Thali Set and Other Pooja Items (functional ritual utensils/thalis, not decor objects). Overlap caveat: several decorative-accessory leaves (Diya & Diya Stand / Urli Bowl / Candle Stand / Lantern; Decorative Bowls & Trays / Bowls & Katori / Serving Platter & Tray) share some SKUs across collections -- this is normal Shopify multi-tagging (a product can sit in more than one genuine site nav category) and each collection is reported at its own exact enumerated count, not deduplicated across categories, consistent with how the site itself presents them as separate browsable menu items.
